title: DC-area forecast: Calm tonight. Rain chances arrive Sunday as humidity builds.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Cloud cover increases some this evening with a small chance of an isolated shower. Evening readings slowly fall through the 80s into the 70s.

What's next? Muggier Sunday with a wide range of highs from upper 70s to perhaps mid-80s and increasing rain chances by afternoon. Shower and storm chances continue Monday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Mostly cloudy as humidity becomes more noticeable (dew points rise into the mid- to upper 60s). Lows dip into the upper 60s to mid-70s. Moist winds from the south-southeast around 10 mph. A small chance of a shower this evening and again near sunrise. Confidence: Medium-High

Tomorrow (Sunday): Partly to mostly cloudy with highs anywhere from the upper 70s in cloudier spots to the mid-80s in sunnier spots. Humidity is borderline oppressive with dew points in the low to mid-70s, while a breeze from the south-southeast may gust as high as 25 mph. An isolated morning shower is possible, then rain chances rise during the afternoon into evening with two or three waves of showers and storms possible. They may prove very hit-or-miss, but a couple of storms could be gusty with intense downpours. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Cloudy skies with scattered showers and thundershowers at times in the evening and overnight (60 percent chance). A downpour or gusty storm remains marginally possible. Patchy fog may develop as we dip to very muggy lows in the low to mid-70s. Some spots could pick up a half-inch or more of rain Sunday afternoon and night. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

More clouds kick off the workweek Monday with intermittent showers and storms likely as a cold front moves across the region. A few storms in the afternoon could be strong to severe. Highs reach the mid-80s, while heat indexes reach 90 to 95 thanks to muggy dew points rising to the mid-70s. Winds from the south are around 10 mph, with gusts up to 20 mph. Confidence: Medium

Clouds begin to break Tuesday, with partly sunny skies returning before a chance of widely scattered showers and thunderstorms in the late afternoon and evening. Highs reach the mid- to upper 80s. Humidity eases slightly, but it will still feel muggy with dew points in the upper 60s to low 70s. Confidence: Medium

A few scattered late-day showers and storms remain possible Wednesday, but many areas should stay dry. Partly cloudy skies continue, with highs in the mid- to upper 80s. Winds from the south pick up a bit, but nothing significant. Humidity sticks around, keeping that muggy feeling in place. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 7/10: Some sun, warmth, and moderate humidity start August with a solid day to spend outdoors. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for August 1

A violent 1983 microburst produced a staggering 149.5 mph wind gust at Andrews Air Force Base—one of the strongest ever recorded—just minutes after Air Force One had landed.

Jason Samenow contributed to this report.
